To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the water-soluble, silver(I)-o-oxygen bonding complexes, [Ag(2)(R-ca)(2)](n) (R = S, R and racemic) and [Ag(2) (R-ca)(2) (S- or R-Hca)], were synthesized from Ag(2) O with chiral and achiral camphanic acids in the molar ratios of 1:2 or 1:4.
the chiral and achiraly silver complexes with camphanic acid ligands were prepared and the crystal structures were solved, and their antimicrobial activities were investigated.
the water-soluble, silver(i)-O-bonding complexes with chiral or racemic camphanate ligands are formed by the reaction of Ag2O with chiral or achiral Hca in 2:1 and 4:1 molar ratios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of water-solubilized silver(i) chiral and racemate complexes, which are potentially useful as biocides.
the synthesis of chiral and racemate silver(I) complexes with chiral ligands and their structures and antimicrobial activity.
the synthesis of new chiral and racemate silver(i) complexes with oxygen-donating ligands and the study of their structure, stability, and antimicrobial activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antimicrobial activities of the complexes were not directly related to their structures, but were dependent on the ligands' exchangeability and the coordination geometry of silver(i).
the silver(i)-O bond in the water-soluble complexes is the key factor in their biological activity.
the antimicrobial activity of the silver(i)-O complexes depends not only on the nature of the ligands but also on the coordination geometry of Ag(i) ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the silver(i) complexes with weak Ag-O bonding, which are easily prepared, stable in aqueous solution, and light-stable, have a potential for use as antimicrobial agents.
